name: backdrop
description: Ambient animated light behind a section — aurora, spotlight, grid, dots or beams — painted by the wrapper's own pseudo-elements, so there is no decorative element to hide and nothing to position. Colours come from the theme's accent, info and success; pure CSS, still under reduced motion, gone in forced colours and print.

static.description: Keep the light and stop the movement. Use it for a second backdrop on the same screen, or wherever motion would compete with the content.

--backdrop-color-1.description: The leading colour of the scene (custom property). Pass a colour token.

--backdrop-color-2.description: The second colour — the answering light in aurora, spotlight and beams (custom property).

--backdrop-color-3.description: The third colour, used by aurora's lower sheet (custom property).

--backdrop-ink.description: The colour grid lines and dots are drawn in, at low alpha (custom property).

--backdrop-opacity.description: Base strength of the light, 0–1 (custom property). data-intensity multiplies it.

--backdrop-size.description: Cell size of the grid and dots scenes (custom property).

--backdrop-blur.description: How soft the light is (custom property).

--backdrop-duration.description: Length of one drift (custom property). Each scene scales it for its own loop.

a11y.notes: Decoration only: the light is drawn by pseudo-elements, so it adds nothing to the accessibility tree and cannot receive focus or pointer events. The wrapper is a plain div — the content inside keeps its own landmarks and headings. Text over a backdrop still has to meet contrast against the page colour; keep data-intensity at subtle or normal behind body copy.

notes:
Wrap the section —
…
— rather than placing an empty element behind it. The hero's own background is the page colour, so give a wrapped hero `background: transparent` through its --hero-bg knob, or the light will sit behind an opaque section.
The root clips its light (overflow: clip), not its content's scroll: sticky and fixed descendants keep working.
One moving backdrop per screen. A second one below the fold should be data-static or a different, quieter scene.
Freeze every ambient loop on a page with `--motion-ambient-play: paused` on :root, or slow them all with `--motion-ambient-duration`.
